extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for geometry problem solving consisting of 3,002 high-school geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language, including problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, correct answer, problem goal, and geometry shapes.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu. Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. arXiv:2105.04165v3 [cs.CL], 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data is collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem is also labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes, and further annotated with dense formal language descriptions for both text and diagram.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: SAT-style geometry problems collected from two high-school textbooks available through the online digital libraries McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline, including problem text and associated diagrams.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is divided into train, validation, and test sets with the ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each collected problem is annotated with unified structural descriptions in formal language for the problem text and diagram. Problems are also labeled with problem goals and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its text, diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. In order to evaluate fine-grained performance, each problem is labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes. Each data item is further annotated with dense formal language descriptions that bridge the semantic gap between textual and visual contents. The paper also reports human performance evaluation on the test split using Amazon Mechanical Turk, where eligible annotators had to have a high school or higher degree, answer 10 problems in 25 minutes, spend at least 7 minutes on the problem set and 10 seconds on each problem, and annotators not satisfying requirements were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: There are no annotated theorem application sequences for data in Geometry3K due to tremendous worker labor. Instead, pseudo-optimal theorem application sequences are generated by randomly sampling theorem sequences multiple times and treating sequences as positive if the solver can solve the problem after applying them; the minimum-length positive sequence is regarded as pseudo-optimal.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees collected the dataset. For human performance evaluation on Amazon Mechanical Turk, each eligible annotator must have obtained a high school or higher degree. The paper also asked dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering to answer problems as human experts.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The project with code and data is available at https://lupantech.github.io/inter-gps. The paper states that the dataset and evaluation baselines are released to promote follow-up work, but no versioning, update timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Education level of annotators is mentioned for dataset collection and human evaluation: undergraduate degrees for data collectors, and high school or higher degree for Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators; graduates majoring in science or engineering were used as human experts.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire following research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that current geometry datasets are limited and that Geometry3K is challenging because less than 1% of problems could be solved without the diagram. Failure cases for the proposed system include inaccurate parsing results and an incomplete theorem set. The diagram parser may fail with ambiguous annotations or multiple primitives, the text parser has difficulty with nested expressions and uncertain references, and the symbolic solver is not capable of solving some complex problems with combined shapes and shaded areas in diagrams.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced as a benchmark to assess algorithms' performance on geometry problem solving. It is used to train and evaluate problem parsers and geometry solvers, with official train, validation, and test splits.
